Precious Metals Sectional Committee, MTD 10 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finahzed by 
the Precious Metals Sectional Committee had been approved by the Metallurgical Engineering 
Division Council. 

Platinum dishes of various forms and capacities are used in laboratories. The puropose of this 
standard is to stipulate minimum purity of the platinum dishes and rationalize their capacities, 
dimensions and mass. 

IS 6019 'Specification for platinum dish' was first published in 1971. This standard has been 
revised to modify purity, design and marking clauses. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the 
final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in 
accrodance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for founding off numerical values ( revised )'. 



IS 6019 : 1993 



Indian Standard 
PLATINUM DISH - SPECIFICATION 

( First Revision ) 



1 SCOPE 

This standard specifics the requirements for 
purity, dimensions and mass, finish, design and 
capacity of platinum dishes ( 10 to 700 ml ) used 
in laboratories. 

2 PURITY 

The purity of the platinum dish shall not be less 
than 99'7 percent. Other platinum group metals, 
as impurities, shall not exceed 0*3 percent, and 
other metals not more than 0*1 percent. The 
platinum and platinum group metals content may 
be determined as agreed between the purchaser 
and the supplier. 

3 FINISH 

3.1 The platinum dish shall be free from defects, 
such as scratches, dents and punctures, which 
may impair its appearance or serviceability. 

3.2 As soon as the lusture inside as well as 
outside, of the platinum dish goes off or it starts 
eroding it may be rejected /refabricated. 

4 DESIGN, CAPACITY, DIMENSIONS AND 
MASS 

4.1 The dish shall be so designed as to have 
rounded and extra thick base to withstand heavy 
wear and tear and with or without reinforced rim 
( see Fig. 1 ). The pouring lips arc normally 
provided. 




4.2 The capacity, dimensions and mass of 
platinum dish shall comply with the requirements 
given in Table I.

5.3 Tolerances 

The following tolerances shall apply: 
Top diameter ± 1 mm 
Height ±1 mm

of that specified in Table 1. 



6 INSPECTION 



Fig. I Shape of Platinum Dish 



Each platinum dish shall be inspected for its 
finish, capacity, dimensions and mass. 

7 MARKING 

7.1 The platinum dish shall be permanently and 
legibly marked with the name or trade-mark of 
the manufacturer. 

7.1.1 The platinum dish may also be marked 
with the Standard Mark. 



Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the 
producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity 
to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained 
from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Acty 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the 
course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade 
designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also 
reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirnied when such review indicates that no 
changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of 
Indian Standards should ascertain that they arc in possession of the latest amendments or edition by 
referring to the latest issue of *BIS Handbook' and 'Standards Monthly Additions'. Comments on this 
Indian Standard may be sent to BIS giving the following reference:
